# Jubilees Chapter 19 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Sarah's Death; Isaac's Marriage; Abraham's Testament; Jacob Blessed

---

**19:1** In the first year of the first week of the forty-second jubilee, Abraham returned and lived near Hebron — that is, Kirjath Arba — for two weeks of years.

**19:2** In the first year of the third week of this jubilee, Sarah's days were completed and she died in Hebron.

**19:3** Abraham went to mourn over her and bury her. We tested him to see whether his spirit was patient and whether he would not be troubled at her loss; and he was found patient and undisturbed. In patience of spirit he negotiated with the children of Heth for a burial place for his dead.

**19:4** The LORD gave him favor before all who saw him. He petitioned the sons of Heth with gentleness, and they gave him the land of the cave of Machpelah opposite Mamre — that is, the field of Ephron son of Heth — and they confirmed to him the land and the cave in it as an everlasting possession before all the sons of Heth who lived in Hebron.

**19:5** These things were written in the book that was in Hebron.

**19:6** And Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah at Mamre — that is, Hebron.

**19:7** In the fourth year of that week he obtained a wife for his son Isaac: her name was Rebecca, daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor the brother of Abraham, and sister of Laban.

**19:8** She became his wife, and Isaac loved her and was comforted from mourning for his mother Sarah.

**19:9** In the second year of the forty-second jubilee, in the first week, Abraham took a wife for himself named Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants — for Hagar had died before Sarah.

**19:10** She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah — six sons. The sons of Jokshan were Sheba and Dedan; the sons of Dedan were Raguel and Nabaoth; the sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were Keturah's sons.

**19:11** Abraham gave gifts to the sons of Keturah and sent them away eastward, away from his son Isaac.

**19:12** Abraham gave everything he possessed to his son Isaac; to Ishmael's sons he gave gifts and sent them away from Isaac. Isaac was above all his sons in his father's affections.

**19:13** Ishmael and his sons, and the sons of Keturah and their sons, gathered together and settled from Paran to the entrance of Babylon, throughout the eastern land facing the desert.

**19:14** These peoples intermingled with one another and came to be called Arabs and Ishmaelites.

**19:15** In the twenty-fifth year of this jubilee, when Abraham was old and his eyes were dim and the end of his days was approaching, he called his grandson Jacob — for Rebecca had borne two sons, Esau and Jacob: Jacob was smooth, and Esau was rough and hairy.

**19:16** Abraham loved Jacob, but Isaac loved Esau.

**19:17** Abraham saw that Esau's deeds were evil and that all his ways were perverse, for Esau was not upright in the ways of God.

**19:18** He called his grandson Jacob and said: "Jacob, my son!" He answered: "Here I am, grandfather." And Abraham kissed him and blessed him.

**19:19** He said: "Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan. Take a wife from the family of my father, from his seed — from the house of my father."

**19:20** "The Most High God will bless you — the God of your father Abraham — and he will increase and multiply you, and you will become an assembly of nations."

**19:21** "He will give to you and to your descendants the land of your sojourning — the land of my father — and you shall possess it and dwell in it forever."

**19:22** He called his son Isaac and gave him these instructions: "I am growing old and do not know the day of my death, and I am full of days."

**19:23** "Behold, I am one hundred and seventy-five years old today. Throughout all the days of my life I have remembered the LORD and sought with all my heart to do his will and to walk uprightly in all his ways."

**19:24** "My soul has hated idols and I have despised those who served them. I have given my heart and spirit to observing and doing the will of the one who created me."

**19:25** "For he is the living God; he is holy and faithful, righteous beyond all, and with him there is no partiality and no taking of gifts — for God is righteous and executes judgment on all who transgress his commandments and despise his covenant."

**19:26** "Now I command you, my son Isaac: walk uprightly before him and serve him in truth and righteousness and love him with all your heart and with all your soul."

**19:27** "Circumcise every male in your household; observe to keep the covenant of God that you have entered into with him; and keep his statutes which he commanded your father Abraham."

**19:28** "Love truth and righteousness, hate iniquity and transgression, and keep yourself from all pollution; eat no blood."

**19:29** At this feast Jacob came to his grandfather Abraham, and Abraham loved Jacob greatly above all his sons. He gave Jacob the blessing of the firstborn and spoke with him about what befits the firstborn.

---
*LOGOS notes: Abraham's farewell address (vv.22-28) is a structured testament: autobiographical confession (vv.23-25), theology of God's justice (v.25), ethical command to Isaac (vv.26-28). The transfer of the firstborn blessing to Jacob (v.29) — over Esau — anticipates the narrative of the stolen blessing in Gen 27 but in Jubilees is presented as Abraham's deliberate choice based on Esau's character (v.17).*
